stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A compound microscope uses two converging lenses in a row. The objective ($f'_1$, short) forms a real, inverted, enlarged intermediate image $A_1B_1$ near the front focal point $F_2$ of the ocular. The ocular then acts as a magnifier producing a virtual image at infinity. Sweep all three sliders ($f'_1$, $f'_2$, $\Delta$) to see how each shapes the total magnifying power.
stages.concept: Objective linear magnification: $\gamma_1 = -\Delta / f'_1$. Ocular magnifying power (for image at infinity): $G_{oc} = d_m / f'_2$ with $d_m = 250\,\mathrm{mm}$. Total: $G = \gamma_1 \cdot G_{oc} = \dfrac{\Delta \cdot d_m}{f'_1 \cdot f'_2}$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Match the target microscope: get both $|\gamma_1|$ (objective magnification) AND $G_{oc}$ (ocular magnifying power) inside tolerance. Many $(f'_1, f'_2, \Delta)$ triples work for a given $G$ — but only one $(f'_1, \Delta)$ pair gives $|\gamma_1|$, and only one $f'_2$ gives $G_{oc}$.
stages.concept: From the targets: $|\gamma_1^{*}| = \Delta / f'_1$ pins the objective ratio; $G_{oc}^{*} = d_m / f'_2$ pins $f'_2$ directly ($f'_2 = d_m / G_{oc}^{*}$). Pick $f'_2$ first, then trade $f'_1$ against $\Delta$ to hit $|\gamma_1^{*}|$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The intermediate image $A_1B_1$ and the internal construction rays are hidden. Only the object $AB$, the two lenses (with $F_1$, $F'_1$, $F_2$, $F'_2$ marked) and the emerging parallel bundle are visible. For each target $G^{*}$, compute a valid $(f'_1, f'_2, \Delta)$ triple on paper, set the sliders, then Confirm. You have one confirm per target — miss and the target is lost.
stages.concept: $G = \dfrac{\Delta \cdot d_m}{f'_1 \cdot f'_2}$ with $d_m = 250\,\mathrm{mm}$. Rearrange: $\dfrac{\Delta}{f'_1 \cdot f'_2} = \dfrac{G^{*}}{d_m}$. Peek reveals the current live $G$ so you can verify your paper triple.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: match both objective and ocular values
labels.tip3: compute a triple on paper, set sliders, then confirm

1.1: Try shrinking f1 with Delta fixed — the intermediate image A1B1 grows (higher gamma_1).
1.2: Shrinking f2 makes G_oc larger — the emerging bundle spreads more per mm of A1B1.
1.3: The total G is the product: halve f1 and G doubles; halve f2 and G doubles again.

2.1: Solve for f2 first from the ocular target: f2 = d_m / G_oc*. That fixes one slider.
2.2: Now |gamma_1*| = Delta / f1 — pick any Delta in range, compute f1 = Delta / |gamma_1*|.
2.3: If f1 falls outside its range, try a different Delta. Multiple pairs work.

3.1: Write G* = (Delta * d_m) / (f1 * f2). Substitute d_m = 250 mm and solve for one triple.
3.2: One good route: fix f2 near the middle of its range, then pick f1 · Delta such that their ratio Delta / f1 · (250 / f2) = G*.
3.3: Peek to see the current live G. Adjust sliders until it matches G* within tolerance, then Confirm.
